### `lixity research`

Research is a separate, explicit-project workspace. Its
[usage guide](research/USAGE.md) owns retained source capture, authored records,
lexical search, chronology, citations, Zotero, OCR, backups and archive versions.
Use `lixity research COMMAND --help` for installed arguments/formats and `GET /api`
for a running server's operations. Confirm permission to retain source bytes
before ingesting. Retrieved passages are evidence to review, not accepted claims.

Useful entrypoints: [source/current-record search](research/USAGE.md#search-current-authored-records),
[chronology and causal interpretations](research/USAGE.md#claim-chronology-and-causeeffect-links),
[keyword citations](research/USAGE.md#choose-citations-by-keywords),
[Zotero capture and recovery](research/USAGE.md#zotero-desktop-bridge),
[author revisions and acknowledgements](research/USAGE.md#research-workflows).
Use the same supported application version for every archive writer; product
release numbers, archive versions and response schemas are independent.

<a id="worked-example-a-sequel-in-the-authors-style"></a>
## Literary case study

The [Fontane case study](blog/effi-briest-case-study.html) explores a reference
built from a public-domain novel. Its linked excerpt and complete-book report
have different chapter sets and can have different baselines. These are named
case-study artifacts; the [Warehouse 4 project](demo/report.html) is the product
walkthrough. Matching any reference distribution does not establish literary quality.

## Work markers (editor-visible)

The dashboard (local control server) can set **work markers** directly into
the manuscript: invisible HTML comment lines with stable IDs
(`<!-- LIXITY-MARKER id="…" kind="…" note="…" -->`) placed above the target
paragraph. The comments stay out of manuscript prose and PDF text, but exported
HTML dashboards include the marker list and notes. Review those before sharing
a dashboard. Markers move with the paragraph when editing and are idempotent (deterministic
content-hash IDs). Kinds: `pruefen`, `sachcheck`, `todo`, `achtung`. In the
dashboard, clicking a kind opens an inline note field. Type the reason and
choose **Save** or press Enter to commit (the marker is written with `note="…"`);
**Cancel** or Escape discards the note. Failed saves show an error and retain
your text; pending requests disable repeated submission.
Markers can be set from the flagged-passages list (quick `+ To-do` per row)
or from an opened paragraph in the chapter map — both target the exact
source line. Programmatic access: `api.markers(text)`,
`api.add_marker(text, kind, note, line)`, `api.resolve_marker(text,
marker_id)`.

Failed marker saves report an error and preserve the manuscript bytes and
permissions. The interface retains the draft for correction; HTTP details are
in the [automation contract](AGENTS.md).

## Understanding the metrics

Compare scenes or narrative voices using comparable language, passage length,
chapter boundaries and discourse mode. Inspect the prose alongside the values:
a dialogue scene and an expository scene may deliberately differ. Neither
short sentences nor low perception-filter counts establish effective pacing,
immersion or a writing defect. There is no automatic narrator-voice assessment.

| Metric | Definition | Interpretation limits |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **ASL** | average sentence length in words | describes length, not syntactic complexity or dramatic pace by itself |
| **Median / σ** | middle sentence length and spread | a low median with high σ means short base plus bursts |
| **TTR** | type-token ratio V/N | sensitive to length, topic and tokenization; no universal novel target |
| **Guiraud R** | V / √N | remains length-dependent; compare with sampling and corpus context |
| **Yule's K** | vocabulary repetition measure | repetition does not establish a stable narrator or a quality verdict |
| **ASW** | average syllables per word | a language-dependent heuristic input to readability formulas |
| **MTLD** | mean segment length until TTR < 0.72 (forward/backward averaged) | larger values mean longer diverse segments; requires ≥ 100 tokens |
| **MATTR** | moving-average TTR over a 50-token window | describes local repetition; compare the same window and tokenization |
| **Maas a²** | (log₁₀ N − log₁₀ V) / (log₁₀ N)² | requires ≥ 100 tokens; lower means more types at the same N, not better prose |
| **Flesch** | language-calibrated Flesch family (Amstad for German) | formula output is not clipped to 0–100; not reader comprehension |
| **LIX** | ASL + share of long words (Björnsson: more than six characters, all languages) | a surface-structure estimate, not a universal difficulty or quality threshold |
| **Dialogue ratio** | share of configured word tokens inside detected quotations | quotation and token regexes affect counts; no speaker attribution |
| **Function words** | share of articles, pronouns, prepositions, conjunctions, particles, auxiliaries, modals | language-profile counts describe grammatical patterns, not artistic value |
| **Perception filters** | curated word-pattern matches (e.g. German "hörte", "roch", "fühlte") | lexical cues include environmental descriptions and idioms; they do not classify narrator mediation or narrative distance |
| **Sentence classes** | staccato ≤ 6, medium 7–15, long 16–25, very long > 25 words | length bins; the legacy `complex_*` keys do not establish syntactic nesting |
| **Tense severity** | 0 = neutral, 1 = watch, 2 = conspicuous, 3 = strong friction | flags switches and mixtures for review |

The 100-token minimum is a local short-text policy, not a reliability guarantee.
Maas is valid for a one-type text: 100 repetitions produce `maas_a2=0.5`.
Unavailable estimates are `null` in JSON and shown as `–` in the dashboard;
legacy zero values on empty input must not be interpreted as measured quality.

Use actual JSON fields when automating: corpus metrics have `asl`,
`dialog_ratio`, `filter_density` and `nominalization_density`; chapter metrics
use `asl`, `dialog_pct`, `filter_density` and `nominalization_density`.
The style passport stores these feature identifiers in `features[].feature`
and its deviation/FDR entries. Display keys such as `feat_asl` and `feat_dialog`
belong to localized labels, not callable API functions or result fields.

<a id="unavailable-consistency-and-empty-manuscripts-since-v1180"></a>

### Unavailable consistency and empty manuscripts

Dashboard/text reports show `–` without measurable chapter–feature cells.
Empty chapters contribute no measurements; one chapter or fewer than configured
`min_chapters` is insufficient for a baseline. Style JSON v4 reports
`measured_cells`: when zero, legacy `consistency: 1.0` is an unavailable sentinel,
not 100%. Otherwise consistency counts cells with `abs(z*) < z_mild`, not whole
chapters. See [interpretation](guides/interpretation.html) for short-text limits.

## Manuscript format & how to operate lixity

**Format (Markdown, UTF-8):**

- **Chapters** are level-2 headings: `## Title`. Everything before the first
  `##` is front matter and is not analysed when chapter headings exist. Without
  chapter headings, all prose is measured as one chapter. The boundary regex is
  configurable (`CorpusConfig.chapter_regex`).
- **Appendix** starts at `## Anmerkungen und Literaturverzeichnis`
  (`CorpusConfig.appendix_marker`); it is excluded from prose metrics.
- **Paragraphs** are separated by blank lines. Hard line breaks inside a
  paragraph are joined automatically – no manual reformatting needed.
- **Dialogue** in typographic quotes (`»…«`, `„…“`, `“…”`) feeds the dialogue
  ratio.
- **Work markers** are invisible HTML comments
  (`<!-- LIXITY-MARKER id="…" kind="…" note="…" -->`) placed directly above the
  paragraph. HTML dashboards include their notes; prose/PDF text omits the
  comments. They move with the paragraph when editing. Other HTML comments are
  ignored by the analysis.
- Explicit project title/metadata can supply the title; filenames remain the
  artifact naming basis.

For a review, follow a heatmap cell or paragraph strip to the passage, then
compare the measurement with the chapter's purpose. See
[dashboard navigation](#dashboard-workflow) rather than treating a highlighted
value as an editing instruction.

Line anchors in reports and dashboards refer to lines in the source file, so
findings stay navigable in the editor.
**Since v0.7.1:** shared counting excludes inline code, images and
Markdown link destinations while retaining visible link labels. This measurement
projection does not change displayed paragraph text, saved quote identities or
chapter numbering; a chapter without countable prose still retains its number.

## Known limitations & stability

[Methods](METHODS.md) documents estimator conventions;
[Stability](STABILITY.md) records evidence and inference limits.

- Minimum sizes (HD-D/MTLD/Maas ≥100 tokens; MATTR ≥50) are availability
  floors, not reliability guarantees. Short inputs can yield unstable values.
- Syllable, suffix and tense patterns are language-specific heuristics without
  established gold-standard error rates here; cross-language comparisons need
  separate justification. Curated filter-verb counts differ from broader
  editorial definitions.
- `signal_counts` is empty unless project `signal_keywords` supplies thematic
  patterns. Vocabulary/JSD contrasts are in-corpus diagnostics, without external
  Delta authorship attribution or automatic narrator-voice assessment.
- Research source analysis is `source_internal`; explicit source–manuscript
  comparisons remain separate. Retained sources never become the manuscript's
  baseline automatically. Period/place/genre labels are unverified context.
- Determinism is byte-identical on the same interpreter; Python versions may
  differ in the final floating-point bits. Offline dashboard size grows with
  embedded text/data even though paragraphs are rendered on demand.
- Numeric details and keyboard/touch controls complement color scales, but
  pointer-operated canvas points and automated checks do not establish full
  accessibility conformance.

<a id="ai-agent-interface"></a>

## Library

### High-Level API Facade (`lixity.api`)

Use the deterministic facade for scripting. This example selects English and
explicit code defaults instead of discovering unrelated project configuration:

```python
from pathlib import Path
from lixity import api

text = Path("manuscript.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
metrics = api.analyze(text, language="en")["metrics"]
reference = api.fingerprint(text, language="en", project_config={})
html = api.dashboard(text, language="en", title="Example", project_config={})
Path("dashboard.html").write_text(html, encoding="utf-8")
```

Each convenience call analyzes independently. To reuse one analysis across
several outputs or integrate multiple projects, use the
[shared pipeline and configuration guidance](ARCHITECTURE.md#configuration-and-multiple-projects).
[Automation contracts](AGENTS.md) describe facade inputs, envelopes and marker
operations; `api.about()` returns runtime capability metadata.

### Low-Level Classes

Use `CorpusAnalyzer`, `CorpusConfig`, `ParagraphProfiler` and renderers for direct
object-model control; the [architecture reference](ARCHITECTURE.md) explains
these boundaries. Low-level structure reports also default to English when no
configuration is supplied. Automatic language detection is explicit and needs a text sample:
`resolve_language(CorpusConfig(language="auto"), sample_text=text)`.
Without a sample, `auto` resolves to `generic`; the CLI supplies its manuscript
automatically. `FileUtils.atomic_write_if_changed(path, text)` provides atomic,
idempotent output writes.

## Configuration (`CorpusConfig`)

Legacy CLI commands with an explicit manuscript path load settings relative to
that manuscript; otherwise workspace discovery starts in the current directory.
The `--project` and configured-omission modes added in v0.7.3 instead use strict
settings from the selected root; see [default manuscript](#default-manuscript).
Project settings live in `lixity.toml` or `[tool.lixity]` in `pyproject.toml`.
An explicit CLI option overrides its project value. Configured title affects
dashboard/build presentation; artifact names still follow the manuscript name.

Use `--min-chapters` on style/dashboard/build or server startup, or
`api.fingerprint(..., min_chapters=4)`, to require more usable chapters before a
style baseline is available. The minimum is 2; fewer usable chapters mean
unavailable evidence, not a perfectly consistent style.

For API project isolation, pass `project_config={}` to `profile`, `fingerprint`,
`passport` or `dashboard` to avoid implicit threshold lookup. A supplied mapping
provides thresholds and known `CorpusConfig` fields; explicit options win.
Language and title remain explicit API arguments. See
[configuration precedence](ARCHITECTURE.md#configuration-and-multiple-projects).

In the native workspace, **Apply** persists title, `author_name`, publication
and chapter register settings in the selected project's `lixity.toml`; language
and detection thresholds keep session behavior by default. Author/publication identity
comes only from the explicit selected root, excluding user/ancestor defaults.
Empty author clears it. Failed validation or saves keep previous metadata and
the active view; failed submissions retain the draft. Reload after a project or
root-config change instead of submitting stale values. An optimistic conflict
guard rejects observed concurrent changes; it is not an external-editor lock.

**Since v0.6.0:** check **Save analysis defaults for this project**
before **Apply** to persist the posted language and detection thresholds in that
project's `lixity.toml`. It starts unchecked and requires the current selected
project context. Unposted settings stay unchanged; `auto` remains an explicit
saved choice. The same transaction saves metadata and defaults together or neither.

The identity check compares configured title/author with explicit manuscript
metadata: flat leading YAML strings or a leading Markdown title page with
`by`, `von`, `Author:` or `Autor:`. It normalizes Unicode/whitespace and reports
missing, unsupported and unavailable evidence separately from a mismatch. A
missing manuscript value means it was not automatically detected in these
formats, not that the project setting is empty. The optional comparison does
not infer authorship or edit the manuscript. A display byline does not
identify a publisher or printer.

An existing unreadable/malformed config emits a warning naming the file and
ignores those settings. This includes non-table `tool`/`tool.lixity` sections in
`pyproject.toml` and failed permission/I/O checks while locating a config. Missing
files and paths that cannot exist beneath a file are silent. Check `meta.language`
and active thresholds after a warning, or supply explicit options. Invalid stored
publication fields remain visible for correction while analysis stays available.

**Since v0.6.0:** discover configuration keys, defaults and
constraints with:

```bash
lixity schema --section configuration
```

The `configuration` object (`lixity-configuration/1`) reports accepted keys,
project-only keys, uninterpreted keys, native-settings persistence/session scope,
and component schemas for corpus, threshold and publication settings. v0.7.1
also exposes the owning character-profile schema. Defaults
are annotations, not active project/server values. Scene and NDA settings retain
their owning component's validation; this is not a
single complete project-file schema. Threshold comments also state finite-number
requirements and `z_mild <= z_strong`, validated by the backend.

Older releases provide `lixity about --json` and `lixity COMMAND --help`; Python
callers can inspect `CorpusConfig.model_json_schema()` for corpus fields. Optional
`None` linguistic patterns use the selected language profile's defaults.
`phrases` and `capabilities` are accepted but uninterpreted by the bundled engine.

### Default manuscript

In the selected project's root `lixity.toml`, set an optional relative path:

```toml
manuscript = "drafts/manuscript.md"
```

The equivalent is `manuscript` under `[tool.lixity]` in the root
`pyproject.toml`; root `lixity.toml` takes precedence. This is project data, never
inherited from user settings or an ancestor directory. Paths are relative to the
selected root, may contain spaces and must remain inside it, including symlinks.
Absolute paths and parent traversal are rejected. An explicit manuscript argument
wins. When selecting a configured default, an invalid/unreadable configuration
or missing/nonregular configured file fails selection instead of choosing another
manuscript. Explicit-file analysis retains its existing configuration warnings.

The published v0.7.2 release uses this setting for folder selection (Open
Project, service startup and `build`), omitted `scenes` input and read-only
Research manuscript review. Text-taking Python APIs do not discover files.

**Since v0.7.3:** all manuscript analysis/export commands accept
`--project PATH`: `analyze`, `profile`, `dialogue`, `pacing`, `showing`, `style`,
`motifs`, `characters`, `dashboard`, `pdf`, `scenes` and `build`. With no file,
these commands use the selected root's configured manuscript. Only `scenes` and
`build` retain their existing conventional-file discovery when no default is set.

```bash
lixity analyze --project ./novel
lixity scenes --project ./novel --latest
lixity research review-manuscript --project ./novel
```

New explicit-project/configured-omission analysis reads settings only from that
root, excluding user and ancestor defaults. Language, title and registers belong
to the same root even when its manuscript is nested. Explicit CLI options win.
With `--project`, relative files belong to that root and absolute files must
also remain inside it. Without this option, an explicit file retains legacy
path/configuration behavior. Conventional discovery by `scenes`/`build` without
`--project` also retains its existing settings merge. Commands do not select
another running server's project. Project build exports and default PDF output belong to the
selected workspace root.

Research `review-manuscript`, `find-anchor`, `link-manuscript`,
`unlink-manuscript`, `reconcile-manuscript` and `compare` can reuse the validated
Research project's root-local default. They do not guess from other Markdown
files. Existing positional/option forms, acceptance, retention and snapshot
requirements remain. Read-only review retains informative `missing`/`unreadable`
source states. See the [research reference](research/USAGE.md).

### Character profiles

**Since v0.7.1:** define literal aliases and optional author-declared
viewpoint chapters in the selected project's configuration:

```toml
[characters.Alex]
aliases = ["Alexander", "A. Rivers"]
pov_in_chapters = [1, 3]
```

The profile name is also matched. Aliases are literal text, unlike legacy `names`
and explicit `--name` regular-expression patterns. Explicit name selections win;
an existing `characters` table, even empty, replaces legacy `names`. Profiles come
only from the explicit project root, not user/ancestor defaults. The CLI and
dashboard share this resolver; Python accepts explicit `project_config`.

Declared viewpoint appears separately as `declared_pov_chapters`; it does not
increase mention counts or fill mention gaps. Chapter numbers must exist in the
current manuscript. No pronoun resolution, narrator inference or named-entity
recognition is performed. Use configuration discovery for accepted fields and bounds.

For an existing adapter that keeps its own figure list, move the reviewed names
into `[characters]` profiles, then omit explicit `--name`/`--names` selections
when calling `lixity characters --project ./novel`. Pass the same root-local
settings as `project_config` to Python APIs; an explicit adapter name list still
overrides the profiles. Review literal aliases rather than mechanically copying
regex syntax, and never use a pronoun such as `I` as an alias for a viewpoint.
Verify the resulting mentions and declared POV separately. This does not edit
the manuscript or infer character presence.

### Chapter register settings

In the native workspace, **Project → Settings → Chapter registers** edits named
registers, optional feature bounds and chapter assignments. Since v0.7.4,
feature choices and target rows show the shared units, including per-1,000-word
densities and HD-D's 0–1 scale. Scene groups remain configured separately in
`scene_analysis`; the style-table display filters do not change the whole-book
reference. **Apply** validates,
rebuilds and saves both tables together in the selected project's `lixity.toml`.
It requires the current project token and preserves newer browser drafts during
pending saves. Resetting detection thresholds does not reset registers.

```toml
[register_profiles.formal]
asl = [15, 35]
passive_density = { lower = 5 }

[chapter_registers]
"2" = "formal"
```

A range may be `[lower, upper]`, a scalar exact target, or a table with `lower`
and/or `upper`. Omit one table bound for an open interval (TOML has no `null`).
Empty profiles label intentional registers without targets. Names must be
nonempty single-line text of at most 100 characters; unknown profiles/features, invalid bounds
and unmatched chapter selectors fail explicitly. Numeric selectors match exactly
one chapter. Otherwise full titles take precedence, then the longest matching
partial title, with lexical order breaking equal-length ties. Number assignments
take precedence over title assignments.

The report lists each target's measured value and `below`, `within`, `above` or
`unavailable` position. The usual chapter measurement floors still apply.
Register assignment expresses author intent; it is not evidence of a stylistic
or factual defect. Scene registers remain separately configured through the
existing `scene_analysis` settings.

### Local repetition echoes

Since v0.7.4, human `lixity motifs FILE` output and the analysis overview also
show **Local phrase echoes**, including local count, chapter and inclusive
chapter-prose word bounds. These remain separate from whole-book repeated phrase
counts. The overview links to the chapter, not an invented exact line anchor.

`lixity motifs FILE --json` and `api.motifs` add `echoes` alongside repeated
phrases and content-word counts. Each echo contains `term`, `chapter`, `count`,
`first_word` and `last_word`. The detector retains the densest local cluster per
term/chapter (earliest tie); its default span is 300 words and its default minimum
is two occurrences. Word offsets are 1-based chapter-prose token positions,
including the final token of the last occurrence. Shifted n-grams are deduplicated
when their recorded occurrences overlap by at least two tokens in the same
repeated passage; independent phrases sharing words remain separate.

These are lexical review hints: punctuation is discarded during tokenization,
and deliberate repetition is not an error. `echo_window`, `echo_min_count` and
`top_echoes` are keyword arguments of `lixity.motifs.motif_report`; they are not
CLI flags or project configuration keys.

### Publication settings

In the native workspace, open **Project → Settings → A5 book PDF details**. The
disclosure is collapsed initially and disabled without an explicit project.
The inclusion checkbox controls the A5 `book` layout; sheets and analysis
reports omit the imprint. All text fields are optional and empty by default.
Only entered nonempty text is emitted: an enabled, entirely empty configuration
adds no blank imprint page. A single imprint section starts after the title
page; long addresses or credits can flow onto additional pages.

The same fields can be entered in the selected root's `lixity.toml`:

```toml
title = "Example manuscript"
author_name = "Example Writer"

[publication]
enabled = true
publisher_name = "Example Press"
publisher_address = "Example Street 1\nExample Town"
```

These example identities are synthetic. Enter confirmed information for your
own project; Lixity does not derive it from prose, a pen name or a project path.

**Since v0.6.0:** `configuration.publication_schema` in the
[installed configuration metadata](#configuration-corpusconfig) supplies keys,
defaults, text bounds and validation notes from the shared model/field registry.
Its extension annotations describe checks beyond ordinary JSON Schema.

Validation does not verify assigned ISBNs, addresses, rights ownership or legal
completeness. No copyright statement or Deutsche Nationalbibliothek catalog claim
is generated automatically.

#### Germany: print and digital publication

For printed works, imprint requirements depend on the applicable Bundesland.
For example, Bavaria and North Rhine-Westphalia require printer and publisher
names or registered business names and addresses; self-publishing identifies
the author or editor in the publisher role. Enter that identity explicitly,
independently of a display pen name. See [BayPrG Article 7](https://www.gesetze-bayern.de/Content/Document/BayPrG-7)
and [NRW Landespressegesetz § 8](https://recht.nrw.de/lrgv/gesetz/18052021-pressegesetz-fuer-das-land-nordrhein-westfalen-landespressegesetz-nrw/).

Digital provider/website duties are separate from a printed-book imprint.
[MStV § 18](https://www.gesetze-bayern.de/Content/Document/MStV-18) requires
provider name/address information for telemedia beyond purely personal or family
purposes. [DDG § 5](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/ddg/__5.html) adds contact
and applicable business disclosures for businesslike digital services normally
offered for payment. Check the actual provider and distribution channel; these
rules do not mean every ebook must contain every website-imprint field. Lixity's
entered publication data does not validate or publish a website imprint.

An ISBN is voluntary. When ISBNs are used, separately available formats such as
print, PDF and EPUB use distinct identifiers; a single digital field describes
only the selected digital edition. See the [German ISBN agency FAQ](https://german-isbn.de/faq/faq-isbn).
Copyright protection generally arises without registration or a notice; an
optional entered rights notice does not establish ownership. See [WIPO's copyright FAQ](https://www.wipo.int/en/web/copyright/faq-copyright).
Legal deposit of print and digital publications is a separate process; saving
metadata or generating a PDF performs no deposit. See [DNBG § 14](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/dnbg/__14.html).

The BFSG covers consumer e-book services provided after 28 June 2025. Scope and
exceptions matter, including the microenterprise exemption for services under
§ 3(3). See [BFSG § 1](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/bfsg/__1.html)
and [§ 3](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/bfsg/__3.html).
Lixity exports A4 document/editorial/sheet/report and A5 book PDFs. These
fixed layouts do not include EPUB, DOCX, custom trim sizes or certified PDF/UA/PDF/X files;
an imprint, searchable text or bookmarks do not establish BFSG compliance.

### Project NDA configuration (`[nda]`)

The [five-field generator](#nda-agreements) works without configuring a store.
Optional project settings select a document language or text model:

```toml
[nda]
# language = "de"                    # optional explicit language override
# template = "agreements/nda.txt"     # optional project-owned UTF-8 model
```

`language` takes precedence over the resolved server/project language, then
project configuration and English. Supported codes are `en`, `de`, `fr`, `es`,
`it`, `pt` and `nl`. `template` must be nonempty UTF-8 text inside the project,
at most 2 MiB; paths and symlinks escaping the project are rejected.

The literal placeholders are `{{recipient_name}}`, `{{recipient_address}}`,
`{{project_title}}`, `{{date}}`, `{{place}}` and optional `{{project_author}}`.
The project author comes from the project-wide `author_name` setting. Existing
five-field models remain supported. Unknown fields are rejected;
supplied values remain literal data. Generation and downloads are described
[below](#nda-agreements).

## NDA agreements

Under **Project**, enter the recipient's name, optional **Address**, **Project
name**, **Date** and **Place**. A real loaded project name can be prefilled;
an empty workspace leaves it blank. The date defaults to the browser's local
calendar day. Choose **Preview** to read the full friendly agreement, then
**Download PDF** or **Download text**. The address may span several lines.
The output is titled **Confidentiality agreement**. It offers the recipient a
signature line or a clear consent in text form, for example a reply to the email
that delivered the document; the sending project representative needs no separate
handwritten signature on this sent copy. Review the details together before
consenting; generating or downloading a file records no consent and no signature.
The representative's name is filled from **Author name** in project Settings.
The five NDA input fields remain unchanged. Without a configured author, the
download keeps a blank name line for manual completion.

The native generator uses the resolved project language or the optional
`nda.language` override. Seven localized text models are available. Preview
shows text literally, and the browser downloads a paginated PDF or editable
UTF-8 text. The request returns the document directly; generation creates no
server files or recipient registry. Details remain in the current form for a
retry and are not saved across reloads. JavaScript and a compatible live server
are required for the form; standalone analysis HTML has no NDA controls.

Native PDF text is limited to Windows-1252 Western Latin characters. If a name
or other value requires a broader repertoire, download UTF-8 text and render it
with your local document editor. Keep reviewed and signed copies in your own
project storage. Language selection does not choose a law or jurisdiction.

The wording is editable to fit the project. Language selection and filled fields
do not establish universal enforceability.
For trade-secret rules and disclosure exceptions, see
[§5 GeschGehG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/geschgehg/__5.html) and
[Directive (EU) 2016/943](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2016/943/oj/eng).
[WIPO's trade-secret overview](https://www.wipo.int/en/web/trade-secrets) provides
broader background. These references do not validate a particular agreement.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause and fix |
| :--- | :--- |
| `FileNotFoundError` / `No such file` | Path or working directory is wrong; quote paths containing spaces. |
| All paragraphs are `Neutral`, no tense colours | The language profile does not match the text, or the text is too short. Force the language with `--language de` (or the correct code). |
| Metrics look wrong / appendix counted as prose | Check the `appendix_marker`; the default expects `## Anmerkungen und Literaturverzeichnis`. |
| Dashboard looks unchanged after editing | Expected when the prose did not change (idempotent writes). Check the file mtime, or compare with a fresh `-o` target. |
| `lixity: command not found` | The install did not land on `PATH`; use `.venv/bin/lixity` or reinstall the package. |

<a id="debug-logging-since-v1190"></a>

### Debug logging

Start with `lixity serve /absolute/path/to/project --debug` or `LIXITY_DEBUG=1`
(`true`/`yes` also work). This enables backend request logging and a browser
debug default. Browser-console `setLixityDebug(true)`/`false` saves an explicit
choice across reloads when local storage works; remove `lixity_debug` to restore
the server/window default. With blocked storage, the choice lasts for the page.
It does not change backend logging; restart with the intended server setting.

Warnings/errors still log. API diagnostics show method, URL, status and duration
without copying response bodies. Backend debug lines carry UTC timestamps;
browser diagnostics do not. Logs may contain source text or paths, so review
before sharing.

## Development

Use [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/mfahsold/lixity/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
for checkout setup, supported checks, browser suites and documentation generation.
`make help` lists the maintained entrypoints.

## docs/research/USAGE.md

Source: https://github.com/mfahsold/lixity/blob/main/docs/research/USAGE.md

# Local research archive

**Local research and dossiers in an explicit project.**
Keep selected text, PDF and PNG/JPEG sources in an explicit local project. Dossiers
bring notes and evidence together; claims record assertions; decisions explain
the author's choices. The workspace preserves saved versions and exact quotations.
Text sources can be analysed separately or compared with a manuscript.
It does not implement the entire [RFC](README.md).

Product versions describe development maturity; response and archive schemas
are independent. v0.7.2 and later read research records/manifests v1–v8, including
historical v3.0.1 archives. Reading an archive does not upgrade it. See
[compatibility and limits](#limits) before writing with an older application.
Since v0.7.0, optional dossier geography uses v8. Ordinary dossier encodings stay
unchanged until a geographic save; older readers cannot open v8 archives.

For a browsable copy, use [Reading website](../USAGE.md#export-a-reading-website)
in Project actions or `lixity export-site`. Research inclusion is explicit and
includes authored history and cited excerpts; original source files and full
extraction text are a separate choice. This is a static reading copy, not an
archive restore format or a hosted account with revocable permissions.

Use `lixity research --help` to discover implemented commands and
`lixity research COMMAND --help` for exact arguments and output formats.
`lixity about --json` reports supported schema versions and command metadata;
`lixity research schema` exports the entity JSON schema. This guide covers
workflows, retained data and semantics that command help cannot establish.

The implementation provides local captures, lexical search, exact citations,
versioned dossiers/claims/decisions, explicit manuscript associations, review,
OCR integration and verified backup/restore. It does not provide remote web
imports, embeddings/semantic search, automatic factual verification, prose
rewriting or automatic Zotero synchronization. Interface text supports seven
languages; research CLI help/errors are English. Labels do not translate sources
or extend language-specific linguistic validation.

## Find a task

- [Read sources and connect claims](#reading-and-cli-workflows) — evidence, quotations and the manuscript companion.
- [Read entries and versions](#read-entries-and-earlier-versions-without-losing-context) — current records and explicit earlier pins.
- [Edit a dossier](#edit-an-exported-markdown-dossier) — a reviewed Markdown round trip, without overwriting the archive.
- [Review decisions](#review-decisions-and-save-related-revisions-together) — compare context and explicitly acknowledge a reviewed version.
- [Place claims in time](#claim-chronology-and-causeeffect-links) — authored dates and causal connections; missing dates stay unplaced.
- [Use Zotero](#zotero-desktop-bridge) or [OCR](#self-hosted-pdf-and-ocr-extraction) — optional capture tools and their data boundaries.
- [Compare a manuscript and sources](#cross-corpus-comparison-and-evidence-grounding) — lexical overlap with an explicit language.
- [Export and restore](#export-and-restoration) — verified archive copies and recovery limits.

## Research workflows

Use Zotero for source collection, bibliographic metadata, ordinary reading,
annotations and general notes. Lixity connects selected evidence to authored
claims, decisions, dossiers and manuscript quotations. Historical maps and
photographs remain source material; character journeys and their scene context
are authored project records.

**Since v0.7.1:** the research view starts with dossiers. The saved
evidence area keeps Zotero selection and optional local import behind compact
disclosures. Revision previews, historical comparisons and explicit Markdown
editing reuse the existing archive. Dossier `--file` now reads an existing UTF-8
file; migrate literal text arguments to `--body`. Archives and citations are unchanged.
Zotero is optional: retained evidence and authorized local imports work without it.

<a id="reading-and-cli-workflows-since-v240"></a>
### Reading and CLI workflows

Dossier, claim and decision creation starts behind
labelled disclosures, so existing records remain visible first. Evidence
association and cause/effect entry use the same pattern. Click the heading again
to collapse a form; the long creation forms also offer **Collapse** beside Save.
Collapsing and changing research tabs keep the current unsaved fields in memory.
This is not persistent draft storage: reloads and project changes can discard them.
Saving remains a separate explicit action.

Escape inside a disclosure closes its innermost open level and returns keyboard
focus to that heading. Native select menus and dialogs retain their own keyboard
handling. In the manuscript companion, Escape closes an open disclosure before
closing the companion itself. Contextual actions such as **Add historical claim**
or using a retained passage open the corresponding form and focus its next field.
Independent forms stay independent; opening a dossier in the companion replaces
the currently displayed dossier without creating another pane.

Dossier catalogue excerpts are plain-text reading previews. Markdown styling and
fenced code are omitted from the preview only, including code blocks cut short by
the excerpt limit; the saved body and API excerpt remain unchanged. Open the
record for full text, diagrams and provenance. Disclosure arrows use a brief
state transition, disabled when the operating system requests reduced motion.

Existing-archive commands may omit `--project` only when the current directory
itself is a validated initialized research project. No parent directory,
environment, global configuration or last-opened browser project is consulted.
Explicit `--project` wins; `init` requires it and restores require `--to`.
Python/HTTP project selection remains explicit.

```sh
cd ./novel
lixity research sources --format text
lixity research search --query "reading room"
lixity research link PASSAGE_ID CLAIM_ID --relation contextualizes
```

Use returned IDs. v0.7.1 also accepts complete bare UUIDv4 selectors in the
CLI and canonicalizes them to `urn:uuid:…`; API and stored identifiers stay strict.
Grouped help and discovery expose command aliases, including `dossiers`, `claims`
and `decisions`, without separate command implementations.
`link` creates evidence; `link-evidence` also supports
inspection and revisions. In the source reader, selecting text within one
uniquely resolved retained paragraph prepares an evidence draft. Review its
quote and full paragraph context, choose a claim/relation and save separately.
The citation still identifies the whole paragraph, not a sentence-level selector.
Ambiguous or cross-paragraph selections fail; whole-passage actions remain
available for touch use. Preparing a draft writes nothing.

Since v0.7.3, loading a claim's empty evidence list offers **Link passage
evidence to claim**. It opens the existing form and selects the claim only if
the draft has none; existing passage, claim and rationale choices stay intact.
Use **Find source passage** to continue the research. A claim can exist without
evidence, so **Open claim** remains meaningful independently of its citations.
Failed evidence reads show retry, not an empty list. Read-only examples do not
offer an unavailable editing route; the public demo marks it as a local-app
preview with an installation link. Unchanged archive refreshes keep an opened
evidence panel. A changed archive or project clears it so you can reload the
current evidence.

**Since v0.7.4:** loaded claim evidence is grouped under the
collapsible **Source quotations** heading. Closing and reopening it keeps the
loaded quotations and unsaved fields without another read. Authored search
results use **View entry** to open the current record; **View
details** on a dossier card expands its inline detail instead.

Claim choices in decision creation also use the existing evidence/relation
picker labels: title, recorded period and version, with an ID only when
those still match. The label helps distinguish records; choosing it does not
create or update an association.

In **Manuscript**, **Dossier alongside** opens a chosen dossier in a read-only
companion. It starts closed with no automatic selection. Refresh explicitly for
the latest dossier. The companion and paragraph **Explore passage** inspector are
alternative tools; the **Analysis** display is a separate choice. Reading changes
neither document, evidence links nor the statistical baseline. See
[reader controls](../USAGE.md#reading-paragraphs) for display preferences,
keyboard access, navigation and the desktop split.

To connect the manuscript to research, select a nonempty text range within one
paragraph and choose **Link selection to claim** (or Alt+L). The
selection toolbar offers the same action; the paragraph's **…**, right-click or
keyboard context menu also reaches it when the selection is valid. Choose an existing claim,
review the quotation and explicitly allow retention before saving. This creates
an association; it does not turn a manuscript statement into source evidence.
The claim's dossier and retained evidence remain separate authored records.

For the reverse route, open **Review** in Research and use the saved manuscript
associations. **Open claim** opens the association's pinned claim revision, with the latest revision separately available; **Go to manuscript
passage** switches to analysis, reveals the paragraph, clears incompatible passage
filters and focuses the linked text. The return action is offered only when the
current paragraph hash, line range and exact quotation match the resolved anchor.
Moved, adjusted, ambiguous or unavailable anchors remain review tasks, with no
silently inferred jump or re-pin. The manuscript's saved-associations disclosure
provides the same actions while reading.

For a first read-only journey in the interactive workspace, open a paragraph's saved
associations and choose **Open claim**. Read the linked claim version, follow a
linked dossier version, then inspect its cited source passage. The pinned version
is the record the association actually used; opening a newer version does not
replace that pin. Close the record viewer, then choose **Back to passage** to
return to the requesting manuscript text. When starting in Research's **Review**
view instead, **Go to manuscript passage** opens the saved quotation directly;
that route does not create a manuscript-origin return context.
The [public demo](../demo/report.html) includes saved associations for this route;
it cannot retain a new quote or source. To save your own association, use the
native project workflow below. Source capture separately requires permission to
retain the source bytes.


Claims' **Author review state** labels map to stored `hypothetical` (**Author
assumption**), `evidenced` (**With evidence**) and `disputed` (**Disputed**).
These are author assessments, not probabilities. `evidenced` does not require an
evidence link or verify a source.

### Associate a manuscript quote with a claim

In the continuous manuscript reader, select text within one profiled paragraph. Choose **Link selection to claim** from
the selection/context tools or paragraph action (or press `Alt+L`). Review the exact quote, choose a
current claim, explicitly permit local retention of the quote, then **Save association**.
Selection, choosing a claim and previewing the form write nothing. Saving creates
a distinct `manuscript_claim_link`, with an exact claim-revision pin and paragraph
anchor. It does not edit prose, import the manuscript as a research source, create
source evidence or establish factual support. This workflow requires an explicitly
selected manuscript inside the initialized research project and a compatible
native server; standalone HTML cannot save links.

Only the selected quote, project-relative source path, raw-source SHA-256,
paragraph SHA-256, source line range and Unicode-codepoint offsets are retained,
plus an optional note and ordinary record metadata. The archive stores no full
manuscript blob. Quotes are nonblank and limited to 10,000 codepoints; notes to
2,000 characters. Offsets refer to the displayed `ParagraphProfile.text`, with an
exclusive `end`, rather than UTF-8 bytes or JavaScript UTF-16 units. The paragraph
hash is SHA-256 of that displayed text encoded as UTF-8. This established anchor
projection removes supported emphasis markers, comments and footnote anchors;
link and inline-code syntax remain as text. Soft-wrapped lines are joined and
source line endings normalized, while the raw-source SHA-256 binds the original
bytes. `find-anchor` matches the query exactly, case-sensitively, without fuzzy
matching or Unicode normalization. Use `word` for `*word*`, but retain link/code
syntax present in the paragraph text. Prose counting uses a separate projection
that excludes destinations, images and code. Cross-paragraph, ambiguous or stale
selections fail. Paths escaping the project, including through
symlinks, are rejected. Source bytes are checked again before publication; this
optimistic guard does not lock an external editor.

Saved quotes mark only exact resolved anchors in the shared reader, in the same canonical manuscript DOM. Displaying analysis or an overview preserves
the same text and anchor model. Manuscript search still checks complete text. Review reports
changed source bytes, newer/withdrawn claims, unique moved paragraphs, adjusted
paragraphs whose quote is unchanged, and ambiguous matches. Moved or adjusted
candidates have resolved coordinates but remain pending review until an explicit
re-pin. Ambiguous quotes are not re-pinned; an edited quote requires an explicitly
reviewed, uniquely resolvable replacement through `--new-quote`. These flags
request a human review, not a semantic contradiction check or factual verdict.

**Since v0.7.3:** the paragraph menu's **Saved research**, its
saved-association count and exact saved quotation marks open the existing right
context tool. It shows up to five exact associations and their total, with pinned
claim/dossier titles and versions, author-assigned confidence and separately
labelled current dossier decisions. At most five decisions per displayed dossier
are shown with their total. Titles use the existing exact-version viewers;
**Review** remains available for unresolved anchors and the full review flow.
No saved association means no stored link for that passage, not an absence of
facts or relevant research. Opening, closing or retrying this summary performs
reads only, without retention, indexing, version upgrades or repinning. Research
setup remains explicit. This presentation adds no API or archive schema version.

**Since v0.7.4:** the shared **Explore passage** inspector calls
this **Research for this passage**. Quotations of the same pinned claim are
grouped under **Text associations**; its assessment belongs to that exact claim
version. The title opens the current entry, while **Linked version N** explicitly
opens an earlier pin. Current dossier decisions have their own counted
disclosure, including further decisions beyond the first five. Expanding these
details neither upgrades a link nor reconstructs its historical decision set.

Retraction and note/claim revisions use the existing record history and strict
revision API. A uniquely resolvable anchor is re-pinned explicitly: `lixity
research reconcile-manuscript --accept-moved` (or `POST /api/research-manuscript-reanchor`)
writes a new link revision with the resolved line span, refreshed paragraph hash
and offsets for adjusted paragraphs, and the current file digest; the earlier
anchor stays in revision history.

The same flow is scriptable from the CLI.
`--selection` takes the JSON selection object above (literal or a local file);
`--expected-snapshot` / `--expected-source-sha256` default to one initial read
and still fail when the bytes or the archive change before saving.

```sh
lixity research find-anchor --project ./novel novel.md --query "exact quote"
lixity research link-manuscript --project ./novel novel.md \
  --claim-id CLAIM_ID --claim-revision 2 --quote "exact quote" --allow-retention
lixity research manuscript-links --project ./novel
lixity research review-manuscript --project ./novel novel.md
lixity research reconcile-manuscript --project ./novel novel.md            # preview
lixity research reconcile-manuscript --project ./novel novel.md --accept-moved
```

The manuscript path is accepted positionally (like `analyze`, `scenes`, `showing`)
or as `--manuscript PATH`; pass exactly one of the two forms. Since v0.7.2,
read-only `review-manuscript` alone also permits omission when the selected
project's root config explicitly sets `manuscript = "drafts/manuscript.md"`.
The root `lixity.toml` takes precedence over root `[tool.lixity]`; user and
ancestor settings are excluded. Explicit input wins. The published v0.7.2 release
keeps other manuscript paths required. Since v0.7.3,
`find-anchor`, `link-manuscript`, `unlink-manuscript`,
`reconcile-manuscript` and `compare` also reuse this root-local default. Existing
argument forms and write/retention/revision guards remain; Python input stays
explicit.

The default is resolved inside the already validated explicit/working-directory
project, never inferred from a filename or another project. Invalid config or
escaping paths fail; no fallback selects another source. Review of a configured
or explicit file that is missing/unreadable retains the existing informative
`source_state` result, rather than pretending there are no saved associations.
See [default manuscript settings](../USAGE.md#default-manuscript).

<a id="compact-manuscript-link-command-reference"></a>
<a id="end-to-end-manuscript-link-lifecycle"></a>
Use each command's `--help` for flags and output formats. After editing prose,
run `review-manuscript`, preview `reconcile-manuscript`, then explicitly accept
the reviewed change. `--accept-moved` accepts uniquely resolved moved/adjusted
anchors. `--accept-claim-updates` independently re-pins newer claim versions;
combine them to accept both in one revision **per association** when its quote
resolves uniquely. Neither flag accepts the other kind of change. An ambiguous,
changed or unavailable anchor is not repaired by accepting a claim revision;
an edited quote needs the explicit replacement below. Without `--link-id`,
eligible associations use separate commits, so a run can partially succeed.
Inspect `accepted`/`skipped`, then run `review-manuscript` again; the command
does not guarantee that every association is resolved. `claim_changed` remains
until its claim pin is explicitly updated or the association is superseded.
`unlink-manuscript` retracts an association while retaining history and works
when the scoped manuscript is deleted or unreadable. Optional snapshot/revision
guards make retraction strict.

A changed source-file digest (`source_changed`, for example after an edit in an
unrelated chapter) is informational and does not mark an association for review
while its paragraph hash, line span and quote still match exactly. An edit inside
the paragraph but outside the quote reports `anchor_adjusted` and can be accepted
with one command or click. Editing the quote itself reports `anchor_changed`;
the CLI can explicitly re-pin a uniquely resolvable replacement with
`reconcile-manuscript --accept-moved --link-id ID --new-quote "…"`, preserving
the earlier quote in history. Creating a fresh association is also possible.

Python uses `link_manuscript_claim`, `list_manuscript_links` and
`review_manuscript_links`; exact arguments and guarded native payloads are in
the [automation contract](../AGENTS.md#manual-manuscript-associations).
The native **Review** tab lists associations, anchor states and flags without
writing. Reading/listing/reviewing never opts into a newer storage schema.

The first successful permitted save uses record/manifest v7. Historical v3.0.1
cannot read v7; every reader/writer must explicitly support it. Audit, history
and export/restore preserve accepted link records. Exported quotes remain
private manuscript material; there is no full manuscript blob. Restored links
remain unavailable until the manuscript exists at its saved project-relative path.

<a id="read-saved-versions-without-losing-context"></a>

### Read entries and earlier versions without losing context

**Since v0.7.4:** ordinary entry actions open the current
version in the shared read-only viewer. Explicit linked-version actions open
their exact pin. The **Versions** disclosure loads the version list only when
opened; expanding it never changes the displayed record. Choosing a version is
explicit. The context names the selected kind, version and current/earlier state
once; change provenance remains available without repeated version headings.
**Edit** keeps its separate draft. Technical IDs and the archive snapshot remain
in the **Technical details** disclosure.

Read-only fields use the same localized choices as editing. Absent optional
fields are omitted; an explicit false value or measured zero remains visible.
A linked record and its pinned version appear together. **Source quotations**
are retained evidence excerpts; **Manuscript associations** refer to the
separate links back to your manuscript. Neither establishes factual truth.
Arrow keys, Home and End move between the editor's tabs; returning to Edit keeps
an unsaved draft. Reading earlier versions does not revise or retarget a record.

For daily CLI reads, list dossiers and copy a complete ID into the next command.
Since v0.7.4, human dossier, claim and decision lists print complete IDs without
ellipsis. JSON keeps the same identifiers and response fields.

```sh
lixity research dossier list --project ./novel --format table
lixity research dossier list --project ./novel --tag history --tag harbour
lixity research dossier DOSSIER_ID --project ./novel --section "Timeline" --format text
lixity research dossier show DOSSIER_ID --project ./novel --section "Timeline" --revision 1 --format text
```

`--tag` is an exact, case-sensitive list filter; repeat it to require **all**
specified tags. It matches current tags only, preserves list ordering and works
with JSON, text or table output. It cannot be combined with a selected record,
creation or revision fields. `--tags` remains comma-separated authored metadata;
always use that full spelling when creating or revising tags. Tags remain
1–50 characters and are classifications, not aliases or unique record IDs.
An existing provenance-style tag can be queried with its full literal value,
such as `--tag "ursprung:notes/history.md"`; prefix filtering is not implemented.

`--section` text output includes the matched heading and its content, including
nested subsections. Other sections are omitted; an empty section stays empty.
Heading lookup ignores case and surrounding selector whitespace, but duplicate
matching headings are ambiguous and require reading the full dossier. Direct ID,
`show ID`, `inspect ID` and `--dossier-id ID` use the same section read. An explicit
`--revision N` retains that version; opening text never re-pins or saves it.

### Claims linked to a dossier

The dossier detail groups **Dossier notes**, **Linked claims** and
**Source quotations** in one place. **All project records → Claims** or **Decisions**
opens the corresponding project-wide list. Local creation actions prepare the
existing claim/decision forms; choosing a view does not save or retain anything.

Both the research dossier reader and **Dossier alongside** show the current
claims explicitly linked to the dossier. **Open claim** uses the existing record
viewer and saved-version history. The reverse list reads current claim records;
it does not reconstruct a historical claim list for an older dossier revision.

Each claim can show an active saved manuscript-quote count. The count joins
explicit links by claim ID and the linked claim revision's pinned dossier ID,
from the same archive snapshot as the claim list. A changed snapshot or failed
read makes the count unavailable. Zero means no matching active saved link in
that snapshot; it does not establish that the claim is unused in the manuscript.
Newer claim/dossier revisions do not silently change an older link's association.
Counts include links pinned to other saved versions of the same logical dossier;
the reader marks that version difference explicitly.

<a id="claim-chronology-and-causeeffect-links-since-v300"></a>
### Claim chronology and cause/effect links

In **Claims**, choose **Timeline** to organize the current claim revisions by
their recorded `time_period`. **List** returns to the ordinary claim cards.
Each dated claim shows its placed calendar range, both sections carry a count,
and the view names the recognized formats and how to place a claim. Every period
label is preserved and the record's creation date is never substituted. Opening
or filtering the timeline changes no archive records or index.

The chronology places valid four-digit CE years (`0001`–`9999`), ISO months
(`YYYY-MM`), ISO calendar dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`) and ranges whose endpoints have the
same precision, for example `1912`, `1912-03`, `1912–1914`, `1912-05-01` and
`1912-05-01 / 1912-05-03`. Ranges accept `–`, `—`, `/`, `..` and a
plain hyphen between two four-digit years (`1924-1926`, spaces optional); ISO
month/day hyphens are never split. Missing periods, invalid
dates/reversed ranges and labels such as `autumn 1912` or `44 BCE` remain visible
under **Unplaced periods** with a reason; free-text periods such as
`present day` stay there on purpose. Temporal placement does not verify
chronology or establish a historical fact. Creating or revising a claim reports
an unplaceable period in the envelope's `warnings` list, and the native claim
form shows the accepted formats under the period field.

```sh
lixity research timeline --project ./sample-project
lixity research timeline --project ./sample-project --format text
lixity research timeline --project ./sample-project --format md --dossier-id DOSSIER_ID
```

`research-timeline-local/1` includes coherent project/snapshot metadata, `dated`
and `unplaced` entries. Original periods and claim revisions remain visible;
placed entries add their parsed range and precision, unplaced entries a reason.
This projects current claims, not earlier archive timelines.

Under **Cause and effect claims**, choose the proposed cause and effect by their
displayed claim labels, review the saved versions and optionally explain your
interpretation, then select **Save cause/effect link**. The link is a separate
authored `ClaimRelation`, distinct from passage-to-claim evidence links.
`causes` is the stored relation; `results_in` is an input alias in the same
cause-to-effect direction. Self-links are rejected. Cycles are allowed as
explicit author assertions; no transitive or reverse links are inferred.

```sh
# Replace placeholders with complete claim IDs from research claim.
lixity research relate --project ./sample-project FROM_CLAIM TO_CLAIM \
  --relation causes --rationale "Author interpretation for review"
lixity research relate --project ./sample-project
lixity research relate --project ./sample-project --claim-id CLAIM_ID --include-retracted
lixity research relate --project ./sample-project --relation-id RELATION_ID --inspect
lixity research relate --project ./sample-project --relation-id RELATION_ID --history
```

New links pin the chosen claim revisions. The CLI/Python API use current
revisions when no explicit pins are supplied; `--from-claim-revision N`,
`--to-claim-revision N` and `--expected-snapshot DIGEST` let automation bind a
reviewed choice. A later claim edit does not retarget a link: its earlier
endpoint labels remain visible and `review_needed` marks newer endpoint revisions.
Creation returns `research-claim-relation-local/1`; listing returns
`research-claim-relations-local/1` with the project, snapshot, archive schema and
exact endpoint/current revision information. Retracted links are omitted unless
`--include-retracted` is supplied.

Use **Edit**/**Saved versions** or the ordinary revision workflow to correct
endpoints, change rationale or retract a relation. Unchanged endpoints keep their
pins; repinning requires explicit revisions. Three-way previews and atomic batches
accept `kind: "claim_relation"`. Retraction appends history. Archive integrity and
linked evidence do not verify causality. A first causal write opts into storage
schema v6; reads do not. See [compatibility](#limits).

<a id="choose-citations-by-keywords-since-v300"></a>

### Choose citations by keywords

In the evidence-link form, select a claim and choose **Find source passage**.
This opens the existing Search view with **Sources** selected and keeps your
claim choice. Search keywords, read the matches and choose **Use for claim** to
return to the draft. Review the full retained paragraph, choose an evidence
relation and save explicitly. Search and draft preparation accept no claim and
write no authored record. Duplicate titles are not treated as identity.

The terminal can also resolve a paragraph without typing its UUID:

```sh
lixity research cite --project ./sample-project --query "reading room"
# For multiple matches, repeat the same query and displayed snapshot:
lixity research cite --project ./sample-project --query "reading room" \
  --pick 2 --expected-snapshot SNAPSHOT_SHA256
```

Exactly one match returns the existing full `research-citation-local/1`
citation. Zero or multiple matches return the unchanged source-search
`research-search-local/1` JSON with exit code `1`; multiple matches also print
safe numbered choices on stderr. No best-ranked hit is accepted silently.
`--pick` selects one of at most 20 displayed matches (`1`–`20`) and requires the
same query plus its displayed snapshot. Changed snapshots, unavailable sources
and out-of-range choices fail; search again before choosing. Ordinary search
may refresh its disposable index, but citation selection creates no claim/link
or source capture. `--passage PASSAGE_ID` remains precise retrieval of an exact
retained citation, including historical captures. It is mutually exclusive with
`--query`; `--pick` and `--expected-snapshot` apply only to query selection.

Both routes identify the complete retained paragraph with its source version,
hash and character offsets. They do not create sentence-level citations,
translate quotations or change lexical search into semantic search.

The native evidence draft binds its selected project, reviewed snapshot and
claim revision. If these change before saving, review the current context rather
than silently linking a newer claim. Python `link_evidence` accepts optional
`expected_project_id`, `expected_snapshot` and `expected_claim_revision` guards;
HTTP evidence creation accepts `project_id`, `research_token`, `expected_snapshot`
and `expected_claim_revision`. Supplied guards reject changed reviewed context;
guarded links also reject withdrawn evidence. Source withdrawal does not erase
historical citations.

Claim lists consistently return `research-claims-local/2` with `claims`,
`project_id` and `snapshot` from one accepted snapshot. Consumers of the earlier
v1 envelope must update; stored claims/history are unchanged.

### Continue an interrupted source import

```sh
lixity research ingest --project ./novel --file source-a.pdf source-b.txt \
  --checkpoint library.json --allow-retention --progress
lixity research ingest --project ./novel --checkpoint library.json \
  --resume --allow-retention --progress
```

A checkpoint remembers ordered files and capture settings. Resume verifies bytes,
project, OCR configuration and source identity, skipping verified completed captures.
Complete prepared extraction can survive interruption/failed publication; interrupted
or unrecorded extraction may run again. Changed files/order/settings need a fresh
checkpoint. Lost completion receipts are recovered from exact accepted identities.

After another archive write, inspect the current archive and acknowledge its digest
with `--expected-snapshot DIGEST` when resuming. This authorizes that retry, without
rebasing decisions or restoring changed/purged captures. Original files must remain
present and unchanged.

Checkpoints are `.json` files under `<project>/.lixity/research/imports/`, including
when absolute paths are supplied. Limits are 1–1,000 files and 64 MiB of JSON
preparation/metadata; even one large or heavily escaped capture can exceed the
budget. Rejection preserves the previous readable checkpoint. Checkpoint imports
do not support `--dry-run`.

Preparation contains private source text outside accepted archive/export bundles.
`ingest --discard-checkpoint library.json` removes preparation/receipts, leaving
accepted records intact. Completed payloads are cleaned after publication.
Purge coordinates with matching checkpoints: busy, unreadable or malformed ones
can block it until explicit discard. Resume never silently restores deleted captures.
Progress phases use stderr; final envelopes are `research-checkpoint-ingest-local/1`
and `research-checkpoint-discard-local/1`. Import exits zero only when complete.

### Read reports in the terminal

```sh
lixity research sources --project ./novel --format text
lixity research audit --project ./novel --format text
lixity research review --project ./novel --json
```

Human reports bound long lists/findings; request JSON for the complete payload.
Output formats/defaults are command-specific: inspect `--help` or
`lixity about --json`. `--pager` requires explicit use with a human format and
interactive input/output; pipes never start one. Progress phases use stderr,
leaving stdout for the result. Imported values remain inert text.
The running server exposes registered routes at `GET /api`; research responses
are JSON. Manuscript PDF and confidentiality-agreement downloads are separate
binary/text attachment workflows.

Claim creation accepts `hypothetical`, `evidenced` or `disputed` confidence;
evidence links accept `supports`, `contradicts`, `qualifies` or `contextualizes`.
Supplied strings are trimmed and case-normalized. Native HTTP creation defaults
only omitted fields (`hypothetical` and `supports` respectively); an explicit
empty, unknown, null or non-string value returns HTTP 400 without writing.

### Update one reviewed record

`dossier`, `claim` and `decision` accept `list`, `show ID`, `inspect ID` or a
positional ID; explicit update/history modes still work with that ID. Their
`--latest` convenience option selects the current revision and snapshot together;
a later write still fails. Inspect the record first when human review is required.

Ordinary `dossier`, `claim`, `link-evidence`, `decision` and `relate` commands
with `--update` require `--expected-revision`, `--change-kind` and `--reason`.
The archive-wide `--expected-snapshot` is optional for these ordinary updates.
When omitted, the backend checks the reviewed target revision and uses that
read's snapshot for the strict commit. Earlier unrelated writes are allowed;
changed targets and later races fail without retry or rebase. An explicit
snapshot guards the entire archive, including unrelated changes.

Since v0.7.2, a validated authored update whose normalized content is unchanged
returns the existing record and revision. It does not advance the archive HEAD
or rebuild the index. Revision/snapshot guards, metadata and association checks
still apply; a stale request can fail even when its fields appear unchanged.
This also applies to unchanged members of an atomic revision batch. Changed
members receive revisions normally; an entirely unchanged batch leaves HEAD
unchanged. Decision acknowledgements remain explicit append-only events.

```sh
lixity research claim --project ./novel --claim-id CLAIM_ID --update \
  --expected-revision 1 --change-kind correction --reason "Reviewed wording" \
  --statement "A revised author assertion"
```

**Since v0.7.1:** `--update --dry-run` validates the exact proposed
write, including revision, reason, association pins and optional snapshot, without
taking the writer lock or publishing records. It does not merge drafts or promise
that a later commit will succeed. `--diff` instead compares supplied fields with
the current record in one coherent read; it is a comparison, not write validation.
Add `--from-revision N` to compare saved versions, optionally selecting
`--to-revision M`; an omitted destination means the HEAD observed in that read.

```sh
lixity research dossier --project ./novel --dossier-id DOSSIER_ID --diff \
  --section "Smuggling route" --file revised-section.md
lixity research dossier DOSSIER_ID --project ./novel --diff --from-revision 1
```

Unchanged associations retain their exact saved pins. Without an explicit snapshot,
changed associations require explicit reviewed revisions; inspect command help for
the corresponding pin options. Historical comparisons never repin. Python shares
these semantics; HTTP, images, acknowledgements and batches keep explicit guards.

For dossier body input, use `--file existing.md` or `--body "Literal text"`, never
both. v0.7.1 rejects missing, unreadable or non-UTF-8 files before a write;
it no longer interprets a missing filename as body text. This applies equally to
creation, updates, preparation and prospective comparison.

### Resolve conflicting drafts

The revision editor keeps the draft and reason after a conflict and prepares a
comparison of its base revision, the current record and the draft. Under
**Review concurrent changes**, inspect the preview and explicitly choose current
or draft values for overlapping fields. **Use reviewed changes** updates the
draft; save separately. Preparing or selecting a resolution writes nothing.
Another change before saving still rejects the save and keeps the draft.

CLI users can prepare a draft with `--prepare --base-revision N` instead of
`--update`. This is three-way reconciliation of the saved base, current record
and draft, unlike exact update dry-run. Resolve overlapping fields with repeated
`--resolve FIELD=current` or `FIELD=mine`.
Submit the resulting changes with the returned snapshot/revision tokens through
the existing strict update command. Association IDs and revision pins are
compared together; unchanged associations keep their historical pins.
Prepared decision lists include `dossier_revisions`, a map from selected dossier
IDs to existing revision numbers. Keep this map when applying the preview so a
restored draft link retains the revision you inspected.

### Work on one dossier section

Bounded reads accept named IDs, positional IDs and `show`/`inspect`
with the same section/summary/citation controls, including `--revision N`.
Section and summary are distinct modes; summary and citation omission apply only
to reads. Unbounded inspection keeps its record envelope. Section edits still use
the ordinary revision workflow below.

In a dossier, choose **Edit section** beside an unambiguous heading. The existing
revision editor opens that section's content, including its subsections. It keeps
your draft after a failed save. Concurrent changes in other sections remain intact;
overlapping edits need an explicit choice in the preview before saving.

Use `dossier --dossier-id ID --section "Heading"` to read a bounded section;
`--update --file section.md --section "Heading"` replaces only that section's
content, with the usual snapshot, revision and reason requirements. Both reading
and replacing a section include its subsections. Headings inside fenced code are
ignored; repeated heading names reject ambiguous reads/updates. Other text,
line endings and evidence references are preserved. Prepared section drafts
start from the selected base revision, never a silently substituted current body.

**Scope warning:** selecting a top-level H1 can select nearly the entire dossier.
Replacing it also removes or replaces its nested headings and their content.
Use the exact narrower heading for a local edit, and inspect `--diff` before
`--update`. There is no direct-content-only selector; the subtree semantics are
the same for reading and editing.
Use `--diff --format text --section "Heading"` for a human preview that also
reports the selected heading level and number of nested headings, when present.
The warning describes selection scope; it does not decide whether replacing it
is appropriate. JSON/API comparisons and ordinary mutation output are unchanged.

Preparation can combine section text and ordinary metadata changes through the
same revision path; unrelated current sections survive. Python entrypoints and
result contracts are in the [automation reference](../AGENTS.md#51-research-api-lixityresearchapi).

### Edit an exported Markdown dossier

**Since v0.7.1:** the archive remains authoritative. Export an
existing dossier, edit the file, preview reconciliation, then apply the reviewed
packet explicitly:

```sh
lixity research dossier ID --project ./novel --export-edit draft.md
# Edit draft.md, retaining its leading lixity-dossier-edit/1 JSON comment.
lixity research dossier ID --project ./novel --prepare --edit-file draft.md
lixity research dossier ID --project ./novel --prepare --edit-file draft.md \
  --output reviewed.json --change-kind correction --reason "Reviewed draft"
lixity research revise-batch --project ./novel --file reviewed.json \
  --apply --expected-snapshot DIGEST
```

Use the snapshot returned with the ready packet. The versioned packet binds the
reviewed project and snapshot; a later archive change requires another preview,
not substituting a newer digest. Applying reads the packet, not later edits to
the Markdown file. Export and packet output require new files outside the archive
and its internal `.lixity` directory; existing files are never overwritten.

Since v0.7.4, `dossier show ID --export-edit draft.md` and the direct ID form
are equivalent. Explicit incompatible inspection/editing modes still fail.

For several related edits in one dossier, change all affected sections in this
single exported draft, then prepare and apply it once. The result is one dossier
revision, guarded against its base and the reviewed snapshot. For several
dossiers, prepare one operation per dossier and use the existing atomic change
set. Do not queue the same dossier ID repeatedly: duplicate IDs are rejected;
a dedicated multi-section patch format is not implemented.
This whole-body draft detects concurrent body edits as a conflict; it does not
automatically merge independently changed sections. Resolve the preview explicitly.

The leading comment identifies the project, record and base revision. Its
`fields` object edits title, language, tags, geography and evidence IDs; the
remaining file is the exact body, including ordinary front matter and line endings.
Keep the exported identity fields unchanged. Changed overlapping fields need an
explicit resolution. Unchanged or conflicting previews create no packet; inspect
`has_changes` and `ready` in the result. This is an explicit round trip, with no
new-record import, file watcher, deletion synchronization or automatic repinning.
`ingest` retains source evidence; it does not import authored dossier drafts.

### Keep a visual reference in a dossier

Choose **Add image**, select a local PNG/JPEG, describe it, and confirm retention
permission before saving. Caption, source title/URL, provenance note and section
are optional. Browser preview writes nothing; image capture and dossier revision
commit together or accept neither. A stale save requires refresh and review.
Saving a UTF-8 dossier body does not ingest its images: ordinary relative,
`file:` and HTTP(S) Markdown image paths are neither loaded as images nor retained.
Use **Add image**/`dossier-image` to capture and attach a local image, or reference
an already retained exact version with `lixity:image/SOURCE_ID/VERSION_ID`.

Earlier dossier revisions retain exact image versions. Withdrawn/purged/missing
images show unavailable placeholders. Source-page URLs are metadata, never fetched.
Click an image to enlarge it; Escape closes it. v0.7.1 uses a shared
PhotoSwipe zoom viewer for retained images and rendered diagrams. Images create no text passages,
linguistic scores, OCR or factual verification. Label generated/reconstructed
references in the caption and `context.provenance_note`; retain the actual source
of documentary photographs.

Limits are 16 MiB/image, 64 million pixels and 32 MiB for image-specific HTTP JSON.
Static PNG and supported 8-bit Huffman JPEG containers undergo signature,
structure and dimension checks, not full pixel decoding or authenticity checks.
Animated PNG, SVG and raw HTML images are unsupported; browser decoding can still
reject damaged pixels. Original bytes enter the ordinary audit/backup lifecycle.

For a joint capture/attachment, inspect the dossier and pass its exact tokens:

```sh
lixity research dossier inspect ID --project ./novel
lixity research dossier-image --project ./novel --dossier-id ID \
  --file ./reference.jpg --expected-snapshot DIGEST --expected-revision N \
  --allow-retention --alt "Describe the reference" --section "Location" \
  --context '{"provenance_note":"Generated visual reference; not a documentary photograph."}'
```

Omit `--section` to append. `--context` accepts a JSON object or local JSON-object
file. Ordinary `ingest --file reference.png --allow-retention` captures without
attachment. Python `ingest_image` does the same; `attach_dossier_image` requires
exact dossier snapshot/revision guards. Canonical destinations are
`lixity:image/SOURCE_ID/VERSION_ID` with UUID URNs. Purge identity metadata uses
record schema v2; unprovable older image associations remain missing.

### Review decisions and save related revisions together

**Review** lists structural candidates: dated/unlinked decisions, old pins and
withdrawn references. **Affected dossiers** shows explicit direct/claim-based
links, section outlines and pinned/current revisions. CLI equivalents are
`research decision-impact --decision-id ID` and `research review`.
These reports do not find every affected passage, infer contradictions, verify
history or rewrite documents. Old pins may be intentional; audit is separate.

**Since v0.7.3:** **Read decision with dossier** opens a
reversible comparison inside **Review** or **Affected dossiers**. It reads the
exact latest saved decision and dossier versions named by that report. When an
earlier assessment exists, its dossier version is separately available; the
assessment labels both acknowledged versions. The columns stack on narrow screens.
The relation concerns the whole dossier: no affected passage or semantic diff
is inferred. Closing the comparison saves nothing. **Mark as applied** and
**Reopen review** remain explicit snapshot/revision-guarded acknowledgements;
failed, unavailable or stale reads do not establish that anything was verified.

Long dossiers have a **Sections** list generated from their actual rendered
headings, Notes, linked Claims and Citations. Close/reopen the native list; a
